tips: Keep the egg bowl warm, not cold, and never over direct heat.
Always save pasta water; it makes the sauce creamy instead of dry.

title: Classic Spaghetti Carbonara
summary: Roman carbonara with crisp guanciale, egg yolks and sharp cheese; creamy without any cream.
difficulty_reason: Timing the eggs and pasta water so the sauce turns creamy, not scrambled.

ingredients.line: 3 1/2 oz guanciale (about 100 g), cut into thin strips
1 oz finely grated Pecorino Romano, plus more to finish
Plenty of freshly ground black pepper

steps: Cut the guanciale into thin strips, about 50 g per person.
Grate the cheeses and whisk them with the egg yolks and a lot of black pepper into a thick paste in a bowl.
Cook the guanciale in a cold-to-medium-hot dry pan, with no oil, until crisp like french fries.
Move the guanciale to a plate, leaving a little of the rendered fat in the pan.
Boil the spaghetti in lightly salted water, since the guanciale is salty, and warm the egg bowl over the pot while it cooks. Save the pasta water.
Toss the drained pasta in the pan with the guanciale fat and a splash of pasta water.
Add the pasta to the egg and cheese bowl and mix well. Do not pour the eggs over the pasta, or they will scramble.
Loosen with a little pasta water until creamy, then top with the crisp guanciale, more pecorino and black pepper.
source_notes: From the voiceover transcript; the pasta amount and pepper are estimates.
